title: Applications of In Vivo Functional Testing of the Rat Tibialis Anterior for Evaluating Tissue Engineered Skeletal Muscle Repair
protocol: Ensure that all machines are properly connected.
Turn on the computer.
Turn on the high-power bi-phase stimulator.
Turn on the dual-mode lever system.
Place the animal into the anesthesia chamber supplied with 2% isoflurane.
Turn on the heating element to heat the platform to 37 °C.
Submerge electrodes in 70% ethanol for disinfection.
Locate and open the lever system control software on the desktop.
Change parameters for Instant Stim under the Setup menu.
Create an Autosave folder under the Setup menu.
Input the name of the sample in the "Autosave Base" type-able window.
Enable Autosave.
Select "Sequencer" at the top of the Control Screen.
Open the Sequence Editor window.
Select an existing sequence and click OK.
A protocol list with parameters for frequency, duration of stimuli, and rest time will appear in the Sequence Editor window.
Click "Load Sequence".
Close the window after loading the sequence.
Select "File"->"Live Data Monitor".
A new Live Data Window will open.
Format the screen using the autoscale function or manually adjust the maximum and minimum y-values.
Ensure the animal is in the proper plane of anesthesia before removing it from the anesthesia chamber.
Remove all hair on the lateral side between the ankle and pelvis of the experimental leg using an electric hair clipper.
Place the animal in the supine position.
Ensure the nose of the animal is securely in the anesthesia nose cone.
Adjust the foot pedal apparatus to its far left position using knob A.
Move the foot pedal apparatus to its lowest position using knob B.
Position the pedal apparatus such that the leg lies in a straight plane by adjusting the track knob.
Clean the leg with three changes of iodine and alcohol.
Allow the iodine to remain on the leg for 30 seconds.
Adjust the animal or platform so that the extended leg ensures complete contact between the sole of the foot and the foot pedal.
Secure the foot of the animal against the foot plate using medical tape.
Ensure the heel is flush against the bottom of the pedal.
Verify that the entire foot is flat on the plate without dislodging during testing.
Locate the clamping mechanism to stabilize the leg.
Push the stabilizing pin in far enough to reduce movement of the leg.
Lock the stabilizing pin in place using an Allen wrench.
Move the apparatus so that the ankle, tibia, and femur lie in a straight line.
Ensure the leg is parallel with the foot pedal.
Adjust the course and fine knobs to move the ankle until the foot and tibia are at a 90° position.
Continue adjusting the apparatus until the femur and tibia are at a 90-degree perpendicular angle.
Activate "Instant Stim" by clicking on the orange button labeled "Instant Stim".
Place both electrodes superficially on the proximal end of the tibialis anterior.
Move electrode tips around until spikes are seen on the live monitor, ideally around 0.4 N.
Insert one needle far enough to pierce dermis and barely into the muscular layer.
Move the other electrode around until spikes are seen on the live monitor around 0.6 N.
Insert needles and clamp them into place using a hobby clamp or medical tape.
Adjust coarse and fine adjustments to find maximal force output.
Turn the "RANGE" knob to desired maximum amperage.
Monitor peaks for identical contractile responses at the set amperage.
Adjust the "ADJUST" knob to set the percentage of the "RANGE".
Check force reading around 1.0 N and adjust current if necessary.
Recheck electrodes to ensure they are secure.
Stop Instant Stim on the high-power bi-phase stimulator.
Click "Start Sequence" in the "Live Data" window.
Monitor curves by returning to Control Screen and clicking "Analysis."
Continue monitoring until tetanic curve takes shape around 60 Hz stimulation.
Remove electrodes and wipe clean with 70% alcohol.
Place the electrodes in the covers.
Unfasten the knee clamp and turn off anesthesia.
Remove the animal from the anesthesia gas and place it in the prone position on the heating pad.
Maintain the rat on 100% O2 for a few minutes after turning off isoflurane to keep the rat oxygenated.
Do not return the animal back to the cage until it regains consciousness.
If muscle soreness is noticed upon recovery, give a dose of NSAID as specified by your animal care committee.
Turn off all equipment listed in step 1.2.
Close the software and continue to data analysis.
Wipe down the platform and foot pedal.
Open the data analysis software.
Click on the High Throughput menu to enable analysis of multiple data files at a time.
Select "Force Frequency" Analysis.
Click on the "Pick Files" button and open as many saved data files as desired.
Select "Manual" in the Cursor Placement Method box.
Change the End Cursor timestamp value to 2.
Click the "Analyze" button.
Click on the "Save Table to ASCII" button to save the file.
Open the saved data file in a spreadsheet.
Create an additional column labeled "Absolute Maximum".
Determine the difference between the baseline and maximum values for each sample.
Multiply each force value by the length of the lever arm (30 mm) to determine torque.
Graph the values as a torque frequency curve.
